nodes.action: migrated the schema without a backup
the corruption spread to the backups and took days to repair
took a full snapshot before the migration
the migration could always be rolled back
set up point-in-time recovery snapshots independent of the backup
deployed without running the test suite
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
switched to continuous replication since snapshots went stale by deploy time

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. You got a sec? I need to talk through the schema migration I ran last night.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Uh oh. That tone usually means something went sideways. What happened?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: So... I migrated the schema without taking a backup first. I know, I know. I was rushing to get the new fields in before the feature freeze.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, no backup at all? That's... bold. Did anything break?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, it corrupted a bunch of customer records. Addresses got shuffled between accounts, some orders got attached to the wrong people. It's a mess.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh no. How bad is the corruption? Can we restore from the nightly backup?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's the worst part — the corruption spread to the backups too. The nightly job ran after the migration, so it captured the bad data. It took me and the DBA team two full days to repair everything manually.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Two days. Okay. So what's the plan going forward? We can't have this happen again.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Agreed. I'm going to take a full snapshot before every migration from now on. That way we always have a clean restore point.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a start. But honestly, I'd also look at point-in-time recovery snapshots — independent of the regular backup cycle. That way you can rewind to any minute, not just the last snapshot.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good call. I'll set that up this week. And I'll never skip the backup step again, I swear.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey Priya, quick question — did you deploy the new checkout flow yesterday? I saw the feature flag flip in the logs.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I did. I know we usually run the full test suite first, but the release window was closing and I figured the changes were small enough.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Small enough? You deployed without running the test suite? That's exactly how we got burned last time.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I know, I know. And guess what — a regression slipped into production. The discount code validation is broken. Customers are getting 50% off when they should get 10%.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh great. So we're bleeding money right now. How did that even pass code review?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It didn't. I merged it without review too. I was in a hurry, and I thought I'd catch issues in staging. But staging didn't have the same data shape, so it slipped through.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, this has to stop. We need a hard gate. I'm going to set up a CI gate that blocks merges unless the test suite passes. No exceptions.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: That's fair. And honestly, I want that. I can't be trusted to remember to run tests when I'm stressed. Let's make it automatic.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Done. I'll push the config today. From now on, untested code never reaches production — the pipeline just refuses to build.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Thank you. I'm sorry for the mess. I'll be more disciplined.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey Marcus, got a minute? I need to tell you something about the snapshot strategy.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sure. Is it about the migration last week? I thought that went smoothly.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It did, but only because we got lucky. I took a full snapshot before the migration, like we agreed. But turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What do you mean? The snapshot restored fine, didn't it?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It did, but only because we didn't need to roll back. The problem is the snapshot goes stale by deploy time. We take it at 9 AM, but the migration runs at 6 PM — and in between, we get new writes. If we had to restore, we'd lose nine hours of customer activity.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ah, I see. So the snapshot is a point-in-time thing, but it's not continuous.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about the snapshot being sufficient. So I switched to continuous replication — we now stream every write to a separate replica in real time. That way, we can roll back to any second, not just the snapshot moment.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a much better safety net. So the old approach — snapshot before migration — is gone?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Replaced it. We still take snapshots for archival, but for rollback, it's all continuous replication now. If a migration goes bad, we rewind to the exact moment before it started, no data loss.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. That's the right call. And it means we can finally stop holding our breath during every deploy.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. I should have done this from the start. But at least now we're covered.
